item.title: Als Nursing Hospital Opens: 14-year ALS drive builds specialised facility; 350,000 donors fund care
item.description: In March 2025, the Seungil Hope Nursing Hospital in Yongin welcomed its first ALS patients, marking a 14-year journey led by dedicated advocates Park Seung-il and Sean. This landmark facility, developed with the generosity of over 350,000 donors and government backing, aims to provide advanced care tailored to the unique needs of those with ALS, emphasizing a community's unwavering commitment to enhancing the lives of affected individuals.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Republicans spent more, Democrats won more: Inside the costliest US midterm battle
item.description: In the 2026 US midterm elections, Democrats made notable gains among Latino voters, following a period of prior support for Republicans. Increased spending by GOP candidates did not secure the anticipated wins, resulting in losses in key districts. High turnout from Latino constituents significantly impacted voting dynamics nationwide, with many responding negatively to proposed data centre projects.
item.dc:creator: Shivanghi Payal

item.title: France deploys 70,000 security personnel ahead of fresh nationwide protests
item.description: French trade unions and student groups are organizing a day of protests against rising living costs. The Yellow Vests movement plans a separate rally in central Paris, despite an official ban on gatherings. Nationwide demonstrations have been ongoing for weeks, with participants demanding wage increases and better conditions for youth. On Monday, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu will meet with union representatives to discuss these issues.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: Streamer Feud Over Halloween: Banks slams Plaqueboymax’s ‘whiteface’ stream; questions career slide
item.description: Plaqueboymax’s Halloween livestream led to disagreements with Adin Ross and FaZe Banks. Adin suggested a blackface stream after seeing Max’s crew dressed as stereotypical white men. Max questioned Adin’s respect for Black culture, while Banks said Max’s costume showed disrespect towards white people. Banks also criticised Max’s content, career direction and Super Bowl halftime show ambitions, and invoked Kai Cenat.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Roy

item.title: US offers $20 million reward for information on Iran's nuclear programme
item.description: The United States has announced a reward of up to $20 million for information regarding Iran's nuclear program. This reward aims to gather details about facilities, equipment, and personnel involved with the program. Diplomatic efforts are ongoing to resolve tensions and prevent further conflict. Iran has expressed the desire for negotiations but requires certain conditions to be met.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: US-China trade talks to continue as Washington presses Beijing to honour Busan deal
item.description: China and the US are engaged in ongoing dialogues to foster stable trade relations, with emphasis on prior commitments. US officials expressed concern regarding China's adherence to agreements related to rare earth materials and agricultural products. The latest discussions revealed the US's stance that China falls short in fulfilling its responsibilities under the Busan agreement. Moreover, China dismissed accusations of inadequate rare earth supplies and agricultural purchasing.
item.dc:creator: Shivanghi Payal

item.title: 'Voices in head said to kill Trump': Man with firearms and ammunition arrested near White House
item.description: The Secret Service took Ronny Yordrix Guanipa Chrinos into custody after he exhibited alarming conduct in his vehicle. When confronted by officers, he insisted that he heard voices commanding him to execute President Trump. A subsequent search of his stolen car revealed three guns and additional ammunition. A Venezuelan national without legal status since March 2024, Chrinos now underscores the persistent dangers faced by the president.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Mahajan

item.title: North Carolina student wins top award for free tool mapping wildlife roadkill hotspots
item.description: Aaryan Ghorpade, a North Carolina student, has triumphed in a national competition with EcoRoute, a project that tracks wildlife-vehicle collision hotspots across the U.S. This innovative online tool gathers collision data and produces heat maps to assist transportation agencies in improving road safety. EcoRoute also encourages community involvement, allowing users to report wildlife sightings. Ghorpade envisions further enhancements and plans to partner with wildlife conservation organizations in his state.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Stephen King's Maine mansion becomes a literary archive, with $2,500 writers' retreats next door
item.description: Stephen King and Tabitha have innovatively turned their Bangor residence into a unique archive and retreat for writers. This initiative offers aid and an inspiring atmosphere, allowing selected authors to immerse themselves in their work. The nearby Brown Mansion will serve as an additional haven, benefitting a variety of literary talents, including educators and Maine local writers.

item.title: What led to Susie Wiles' firing within 3 days of Trump's midterm loss? 'Ice maiden' was Trump's longest serving chief of staff
item.description: Susie Wiles fired: Within three days of midterm rout, President Donald Trump elevated Stephen Miller to the post of Chief of Staff replacing Susie Wiles, who served the longest on the post. The decision was not out of the blue as there were speculations which the president at that time dismissed.

item.title: Meryl Streep backs women's history education as two teachers earn award for AP course campaign
item.description: Kristen Kelly and Serene Williams from Sacred Heart Preparatory have pioneered an Advanced Placement course focused on women's history, garnering endorsement from 100 esteemed universities and colleges. This initiative underscores the vital role women have played throughout history. An eminent gala in Chicago on November 6, 2026, will unveil the inaugural Meryl Streep Educator Award, with proceeds dedicated to bolstering educational resources for women's history.

item.title: London councillors reject Berkeley Homes plan after affordable housing offer falls from 40% to 12%
item.description: Southwark Council's planning committee voted unanimously against Berkeley Homes' revised plans for the Bermondsey Place development. The housebuilder proposed reducing affordable housing from 40 percent to just 12 percent, causing strong local opposition. Council members expressed concerns about the long timeline for home completion and questioned the developer's financial figures. Berkeley Homes highlighted rising costs and council fees as reasons for the reduced affordable housing offer.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Court upholds sale of divorced Arkansas woman's property share after her bankruptcy filing.
item.description: In a landmark ruling, a federal appeals court upheld the sale of a divorced woman's stake in property located in Arkansas. The decision favored her bankruptcy trustee, overcoming objections posed by her ex-husband. He contended that the buyer's good faith was not adequately proven in prior hearings but failed to voice this concern earlier. Consequently, the property transaction with Blue Sun Capital LLC is deemed legally binding.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Dallas' star Victoria Principal, 76, now rescues animals on her ranch; shares miniature horse Halo's recovery
item.description: Former actress Victoria Principal has found her true calling in animal rehabilitation, dedicating her life to caring for rescued creatures at her ranch. One notable resident is Halo, a miniature horse currently healing with her support. Principal passionately advocates for the role of love and patience in nurturing these animals back to health, marking a significant departure from her Hollywood days as she embraces her new purpose.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Jackass' star Steve-O turns 44-acre Tennessee ranch into a home for rescued animals
item.description: Steve-O, the famous Jackass star, has dedicated himself to animal welfare by establishing The Radical Ranch, a sanctuary for rescued animals situated near Nashville. Since its inception as a nonprofit in 2024, the ranch has provided a home for nine animals, including goats and pigs. Steve-O envisions expanding the sanctuary to include cows and chickens while fostering empathy towards all creatures.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
